'''Alex Jan''' '''"Lex"''' '''van der Eb''' (born 16 January 1934) is a Dutch molecular biologist and virologist. He was a professor of fundamental [[Oncovirus|tumor virology]] and later molecular [[carcinogenesis]] at [[Leiden University]] from 1979 to 2000. He has performed research in [[Adenoviridae|adenoviruses]] and was fundamental in the creation of the technique of [[Transfection#Methods|calcium phosphate transfection]] and the founding of the [[HEK 293 cells|HEK 293]] and PER.C6 cell lines.

== Life ==
Van der Eb was born on 16 January 1934 in [[Bandung]], [[Dutch East Indies]].<ref name=ul>{{cite web|url=https://hoogleraren.leidenuniv.nl/id/724 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201016150336/https://hoogleraren.leidenuniv.nl/id/724 |title=Alex Jan van der Eb |language=nl |publisher=Leiden University |date= |archive-date=16 October 2020}}</ref> He studied biology at [[Leiden University]] and afterwards attended [[Delft University of Technology]] for a further year to specialize in [[microbiology]].<ref name="putten">{{cite web|author=J.B. Meijer van Putten |url=https://www.ntvg.nl/artikelen/nieuws/profdrajvan-der-eb-over-adenovirussen-en-kanker/volledig |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201016193400/https://www.ntvg.nl/artikelen/nieuws/profdrajvan-der-eb-over-adenovirussen-en-kanker/volledig |title=Prof.dr.A.J.van der Eb over adenovirussen en kanker. |language=nl |publisher=Nederlands Tijdschrift voor Geneeskunde |date=24 June 1998 |archive-date=16 October 2020}}</ref> Van der Eb had to fulfill his [[military service]] upon graduation and asked the head of military health services to be employed in one of the military laboratories. In 1962 he was sent to work as a biologist on [[Poxviridae|poxviruses]] in the virology department of Leiden University. At Leiden he met professor J.A. Cohen of the Medical-Biological Laboratory of the [[Netherlands Organisation for Applied Scientific Research]] (TNO). After his military service ended in 1963 van der Eb became a grad-student under Cohen.<ref name="putten"/><ref name="parool">{{cite web|author=Jop van Kempen, Bas Soetenhorst |url=https://www.parool.nl/nieuws/hoe-nederland-de-kennis-voor-een-kansrijk-coronavaccin-uit-handen-gaf~b1b94267/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200521144821/https://www.parool.nl/nederland/hoe-nederland-de-kennis-voor-een-kansrijk-coronavaccin-uit-handen-gaf~b1b94267/ |title=Hoe Nederland de kennis voor een kansrijk coronavaccin uit handen gaf |publisher=Het Parool |date=9 May 2020 |archive-date=21 May 2020}}</ref> He studied [[Adenoviridae|adenoviruses]] and characterized the virus DNA in 1966.<ref name="synabs">{{cite web|url=https://www.synabs.be/2020/10/06/hek293-when-the-virus-meets-the-cell/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201016194716/https://www.synabs.be/2020/10/06/hek293-when-the-virus-meets-the-cell/ |title=HEK293: when the virus meets the cell |publisher=synabs.be |date=6 October 2020 |archive-date=16 October 2020}}</ref> He obtained his PhD at Leiden University in 1968 with a thesis titled: "Fysisch-chemische en biologische eigenschappen van het DNA van dierlijke tumorvirussen".<ref name=ul/> Van der Eb subsequently moved to the United States to become a post-grad at the [[California Institute of Technology]], where he broadened his knowledge of [[DNA]].<ref name="putten"/>

Upon request of Cohen van der Eb returned to the Netherlands in 1970 to start a research group in molecular biology of [[oncovirus]]es.<ref name="putten"/> During this period Canadian post-doc [[Frank L. Graham]] joined his research group.<ref name="synabs"/> Together they worked on a technique to insert foreign [[DNA]] in cultured human cells. The technique of [[Transfection#Methods|calcium phosphate transfection]] became available in 1973.<ref name="becker">{{cite web|author=Sander Becker |url=https://www.trouw.nl/nieuws/geacht-nobelcomite~b93d2d2a/ |title=Geacht Nobelcomité |language=nl |publisher=Trouw |date=6 October 2007 |access-date=16 October 2020}}</ref><ref name=kievits>{{cite web|author=F. Kievits and M.T. Adriaanse |url=https://www.ntvg.nl/artikelen/nieuws/profdrdbootsma/volledig |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161225144529/https://www.ntvg.nl/artikelen/nieuws/profdrdbootsma/volledig |title=Prof.dr.D.Bootsma |language=nl |publisher=Nederlands Tijdschrift voor Geneeskunde |date=14 October 2002 |archive-date=25 December 2016}}</ref><ref name="Grahamvan der Eb1973">{{cite journal|last1=Graham|first1=F.L.|last2=van der Eb|first2=A.J.|title=A new technique for the assay of infectivity of human adenovirus 5 DNA|journal=Virology|volume=52|issue=2|year=1973|pages=456–467|issn=0042-6822|doi=10.1016/0042-6822(73)90341-3|pmid=4705382}}</ref> Fellow molecular biologist [[Piet Borst]] called this discovery of how to insert foreign DNA in human cells the cornerstone of [[genetics]] and [[cell biology]].<ref name="parool"/><ref>{{cite web|author=Valentijn van der Lende |url=https://dekennisvannu.nl/site/artikel/De-geschiedenis-van-de-gentherapie-een-controversiele-wetenschap/8027 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190510032715/https://dekennisvannu.nl/site/artikel/De-geschiedenis-van-de-gentherapie-een-controversiele-wetenschap/8027 |title=De geschiedenis van de gentherapie: een controversiële wetenschap |language=nl |publisher=De Kennis van Nu |date=17 March 2016 |archive-date=10 May 2019}}</ref> In 1972 van der Eb obtained and managed to culture embryonic kidney cells from an aborted or miscarried human foetus.<ref name="brouwers">{{cite news|author=Lucas Brouwers |url=https://www.nrc.nl/nieuws/2013/04/27/een-mensencel-is-vogelvrij-1238556-a541997 |url-access=subscription |title=Een mensencel is vogelvrij |newspaper=NRC |language=nl |publisher=NRC Handelsblad |date=27 April 2013 |access-date=16 October 2020}}</ref><ref name=fda3750>[https://wayback.archive-it.org/7993/20170404095417/https://www.fda.gov/ohrms/dockets/ac/01/transcripts/3750t1_01.pdf Vaccines and Related Biological Products Advisory Committee Meeting], p.81 Lines 14–22:, [[Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research]], May 16, 2001</ref> With Graham's contributions in transfection of the cells with the adenovirus 5 this led to the cell line of [[HEK 293 cells]].<ref name="synabs"/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://hek293.com/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141016031034/http://hek293.com/index.html |title=HEK293 Cell Line |publisher=hek293.com |date= |archive-date=16 October 2014}}</ref> HEK 293 became one of the most used cell lines worldwide, coming close to the use of the [[HeLa]] cell line.<ref name="brouwers"/> In 1974 van der Eb and Graham demonstrated that loose virus DNA could cause cancer.<ref name="becker"/>

In 1974 van der Eb became a lector of fundamental [[Oncovirus|tumor virology]]. In 1979 he was named professor of fundamental tumor virology.<ref name=ul/> From 1987 to 1992 he performed research on the [[chicken anemia virus]] together with Mathieu Noteborn.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/nieuws/2019/04/in-memoriam-professor-mathieu-noteborn |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201017151221/https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/nieuws/2019/04/in-memoriam-professor-mathieu-noteborn |title=In memoriam professor Mathieu Noteborn |language=nl |publisher=Leiden University |date=8 April 2019 |archive-date=17 October 2020}}</ref> In 1988 his teaching assignment was changed to molecular [[carcinogenesis]].<ref name=ul/> In 1995, together with Dinko Valerio, he created the [[PER.C6|PER.C6 cell line]] with enhanced traceability compared to the HEK 293 line, this time coming from retinal cells.<ref name="synabs"/> The goal of Valerio was to use it for [[gene therapy]] but this was ultimately unsuccessful. In contrast to HEK 293 the PER.C6 cell line was patented by Leiden University and IntroGene (later [[Crucell]]) and used commercially.<ref name="parool"/><ref name="brouwers"/> AdVac later became an enhanced version of PER.C6 and both were deemed to be very useful to construct vaccines with, becoming the basis of vaccines for [[ebola]], [[Zika fever]] and [[HIV]].<ref name="parool"/> Van der Eb retired in 2000.<ref name=ul/> He later worked as an advisor for biotechnology company Crucell between 2000 and 2013.<ref name="parool"/> In 2007 he was involved in writing the behavioural code for [[biosecurity]] of the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web|author=Elles Lalieu |url=https://www.nemokennislink.nl/publicaties/knutselen-aan-gevaarlijke-virussen/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201017162654/https://www.nemokennislink.nl/publicaties/knutselen-aan-gevaarlijke-virussen/ |title=Knutselen aan gevaarlijke virussen |language=nl |publisher=NEMO Kennislink |date=20 January 2012 |archive-date=17 October 2020}}</ref>

In 2020 van der Eb together with two other former Crucell officials stated that the Netherlands would have had a better starting position in obtaining vaccines to deal with the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the Netherlands]] if the government had been interested in letting Crucell work together with the {{ill|Netherlands Vaccine Institute|nl|Nederlands Vaccin Instituut}}, with Crucell offering the Netherlands rapid vaccine production in the case of a [[pandemic]] multiple times during the early 2000s. Crucell was later bought by the American corporation [[Johnson & Johnson]].<ref name="parool"/>

==Honours and awards==
Van der Eb was elected a member of the [[European Molecular Biology Organization]] in 1977.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://people.embo.org/profile/alex-j-van-der-eb |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200918131144/https://people.embo.org/profile/alex-j-van-der-eb |title=Alex J. van der Eb |publisher=European Molecular Biology Organization |date= |archive-date=18 September 2020}}</ref> In 1978 he won the [[M.W. Beijerinck Virology Medal]] of the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://knaw.nl/en/awards/laureates/beijerinck-virology-prize/overzicht |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200719221307/https://knaw.nl/en/awards/laureates/beijerinck-virology-prize/overzicht |title=Beijerink Virology Prize |publisher=Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences |date= |archive-date=19 July 2020}}</ref> He was elected member of the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 1987.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.knaw.nl/en/members/members/4073 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200730103842/https://www.knaw.nl/en/members/members/4073 |title=Lex van der Eb |publisher=Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences |date= |archive-date=30 July 2020}}</ref> He was elected a member of [[Academia Europaea]] in 1989.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Eb_Alex |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190401120842/https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Eb_Alex |title=Alex van der Eb |publisher=Academia Europaea |date= |archive-date=1 April 2019}}</ref> In 1989 he was also winner of the [[Robert Koch Medal and Award#Robert Koch Prize Winners since 1960|Robert Koch Prize]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.robert-koch-stiftung.de/index.php?article_id=15&clang=1 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201010103540/https://www.robert-koch-stiftung.de/index.php?article_id=15&clang=1 |title=Robert Koch Award |publisher=Robert-Koch-Stiftung |date= |archive-date=10 October 2020}}</ref> In the same year he won the Japan Foundation for Promotion of Cancer Research Award.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.njv.info/prof-dr-lex-van-der-eb-in-het-nieuws/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201017152529/https://www.njv.info/prof-dr-lex-van-der-eb-in-het-nieuws/ |title=NJV lid Prof. dr. Lex van der Eb in het nieuws |publisher=Nederlands-Japanse Vereniging |date= 13 May 2020|archive-date=17 October 2020}}</ref> He was made a Knight of the [[Order of the Netherlands Lion]] in 1998.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ntvg.nl/artikelen/personalia-6746 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201016162012/https://www.ntvg.nl/artikelen/personalia-6746 |title=Personalia |language=nl |publisher=Nederlands Tijdschrift voor Geneeskunde |date=27 May 1998 |archive-date=16 October 2020}}</ref> In 2003 he was appointed an honorary member of the Netherlands Society of Gene and Cell Therapy.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nvgct.nl/honorary-members/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200811002722/https://www.nvgct.nl/honorary-members/ |title=Honorary members |publisher=Netherlands Society of Gene and Cell Therapy |date= 29 November 2017|archive-date=11 August 2020}}</ref> He is a member of the [[Koninklijke Hollandsche Maatschappij der Wetenschappen]].<ref name="parool"/>
